pos.personaBrief: Sacchi wanted to 'dominate games' and win 'on merit', using 'short, quick passes' (Vice). Control came mostly from pressing and territory, so the team neither sat back to counter nor treated the ball as its defence.

pro.personaBrief: The team moved the ball forward with quick short passing through Rijkaard and Ancelotti (Gentleman Ultra) and pressed from the front after losing it, so it was vertical and quick rather than patient. Under the pre-1992 rules it did not take risks playing out near its own box.

est.personaBrief: Rehearsed '11 contra 0' movements and shadow play (FIFA, Vice) with positions defined by 'the ball, the space, the team-mate and the opponent' make this strongly positional, but inside a compact 25-metre block. Gullit and van Basten combined freely, and the wide midfielders came inside.

lar.personaBrief: No verified width evidence; from general knowledge, the flat 4-4-2 had no touchline wingers and the decisive players (Gullit, van Basten, Rijkaard) were central, while Tassotti and Maldini gave width from full-back.

blo.personaBrief: This is the archetypal high block: 'an extremely high defensive line', pressing 'as a unit' (Vice), 'aggressive pressing' and an offside trap (UEFA, FIFA), and pressing from the front after losing the ball (Gentleman Ultra).

mar.personaBrief: This was 'a pure zonal system' (FootballTransfers): Milan 'defended zones of the pitch' instead of marking players (Guide to Football), unlike other Italian teams of the time (Vice).

pla.personaBrief: No verified game-plan evidence; from general knowledge, Sacchi imposed his model on everyone, stars included, drilled it through shadow play, and played the same way against Real Madrid and away in Europe. That fits the verified focus on rehearsing the team's own movements.

res.personaBrief: No verified in-period evidence; the attributed quotes say a win without merit 'wasn't a game' and that he sent players out to entertain the public for 90 minutes. From general knowledge, the team kept pressing and attacking rather than shutting games down.

sis.personaBrief: No verified axis evidence; from general knowledge plus the 1987 context (players signed from Serie B and C, 'looked at their head') and the attributed 'players who speak the same language', the collective system came above individual talent and stars had defined roles.

jog.personaBrief: The team needed intensity and constant movement ('ran better', not more), but it valued intelligent, ball-comfortable players: the back four were at ease on the ball and Rijkaard controlled play (Vice). There was no room for a static playmaker.

bas.personaBrief: No verified squad-building evidence in the period; from general knowledge, Milan was built mainly through Berlusconi's signings, while young players such as Maldini and Costacurta were key starters from early on.

lid.personaBrief: A demanding perfectionist: Ancelotti said players never gave everything in training until Sacchi arrived, and van Basten described maximum effort demanded in every session (UEFA). The coach had the final word, stars included.
